newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast prod prices mixed in Tuesday markets.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast prod prices mixed in Tuesday markets.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products were mixed Tuesday, reflecting higher daytime prices for futures amid concerns of increased supplies, dealers said.
Crude oil for July delivery rose 23 cents a barrel Tuesday to $19.23 due to increased refinery buying in other regions.
But the increase in other crude markets was offset by reports of higher supplies in the West Coast region.
Trade group American Petroleum Institute (API) reported West Coast gasoline stocks rose 502,000 barrels last week to 30.7 million barrels.
"The inventories were bearish and didn't give (traders) a lot of encouragement," a broker said.
Trade was moderately active Tuesday, a day after most participants attended a golf tournament in southern California.
The market's mixed messages sent June supplies of Los Angeles cleaner-burning CARB gasoline up 0.50 cents a gallon to 53.50/54.50 cents, while conventional gasoline eased 1.50 to 50/51 cents.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles rose a half cent to 58/59 cents a gallon.
Reformulated gasoline in L.A. and San Francisco was about one cent under L.A. CARB gasoline.
